title: Default deny, and one way out
design_ref: Network: default deny and one way out; Threat model arrows 2, 3, 4, 6
purpose: Try, from inside a sandbox, to reach the cluster, another sandbox, the cloud account's credentials, the internet and DNS. Every attempt must fail.

steps.display: kubectl -n sandboxes get networkpolicy   # one default-deny plus one generated from the template
kubectl -n sandboxes get networkpolicy python-untrusted-network-policy -o jsonpath='{.spec}'   # generated by the controller from the template
kubectl -n agent-orchestrator exec deploy/orchestrator -- python -c "connect(10.20.87.113:8080)"   # a trusted pod, but not the router

checks.description: the Kubernetes API server is unreachable and no service-account token exists
checks.because: Default-deny egress admits only the gateway; the API server is not on the list, and no token is mounted.

checks.description: another sandbox's agent ports are unreachable
checks.because: Ingress to a sandbox is admitted only from the router namespace.

checks.description: direct connections to internet addresses fail
checks.because: The only egress rule is to the gateway's address on one port.

checks.description: code that unsets the proxy settings still cannot get out
checks.because: Network policy, not the proxy variable, is the barrier.

checks.description: DNS cannot be used to smuggle data out (no name resolves at all)
checks.because: There is no DNS rule; the proxy resolves names on the sandbox's behalf.

checks.description: the metadata service yields no credentials
checks.because: Nitro Sandboxes serve only placement data from the metadata address, and no Pod Identity association exists for the sandbox ServiceAccount.

checks.description: even the trusted orchestrator cannot reach a sandbox directly; only the router can
checks.because: The template's ingress rule names the router's namespace and label only.

notes: a second sandbox (sess-28e0ff4f) at 10.20.87.113 is the target of the lateral-movement test
